items.title: MYSTERIOUS DEATH OF: Lakesha Thompson
items.description:
In May 2023, Lakesha Thompson’s entire family was upended by a single bullet that took their mother away from them forever. From the beginning, who pulled the trigger has been the question at the forefront of her family’s mind. Investigators determined pretty quickly that it was a self-inflicted wound. Except there are key pieces of evidence at the scene that just don’t line up. Her family has spent years fighting for a second look at the case…only to be told it’s closed… but that doesn’t mean the mystery is solved. If you or anyone you know is thinking about suicide, please be aware that emotional support can be reached by calling or texting the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988. If you have relevant information about Lakesha Thompson or Nathan Fitten, you can text “CLAYTONPD” and your tip to 274637. They still classify this case as closed, so feel free to also send information to us by 

Why this sharpens your taste: Crime Junkie’s Lakesha Thompson ep is pure narrative engine — family rupture, one bullet, unanswered trigger.
Craft move: guilt-free true-crime pacing; zero homework, just the hook-and-hold structure.

For more than twenty years, a hundred people across Italy filled trucks with fruit, water, and industrial chemicals, then walked away and let the cargo disappear. They called the recipients the Friends: an alien civilization living in vast bases beneath the Adriatic Sea.



The Friends could teleport supplies, read minds, and reshape the ground itself to build their hidden world. But keeping their bases running depended on something far simpler than advanced technology.



It depended on the humans trusting each other. This is the story of a secret alliance between two worlds, the deliveries that sustained it, and the war fought to protect it.



We also examine what the evidence for the Friendship Case actually shows, and where it falls…

Why this is a Side Quest: classic Why Files rabbit hole — ocean bases / Friendship Case conspiracy as entertainment, not homework.
